text: And Job answered and said:
“Listen carefully [to] my speech, and let this be your⁺ consolation.
Bear with me, and I will speak; and after I have spoken, you may mock.
As for me, is my complaint against man? And if [so], why [should] not my spirit be short?
Turn to me and be appalled, and put a hand over [your] mouth.
Even when I remember, then I am terrified, and trembling seizes my flesh.
Why do the wicked live on, growing old, even becoming mighty in power?
Their seed is established with them before their face, and their offspring before their eyes.
Their houses [are] safe from dread, and the rod of God is not upon them.
His bull passes over, without fail; his cow brings forth, and [does] not miscarry.
They send forth their little boys like a flock, and their children skip about.
They lift up to the tambourine and harp, and they rejoice at the sound of the flute.
They wear out their days in prosperity, and in peace go down to Sheol.
And they said to God, ‘Turn away from us! For we do not delight to know Your ways.
What [is] Shaddai that we should serve Him? And what do we gain that we should meet with Him?’
Behold, their own good [is] not in their hand; the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
How often [is] the lamp of the wicked put out, and their destruction comes upon them? The pains He apportions in His anger.
They become like straw before the face of the wind, and like chaff that the storm carries him away.
Does God store up for his sons his trouble? Let Him repay to him, and he will know.
Let his eyes see his destruction, and let him drink from the wrath of Shaddai.
For what [is] his delight in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off?
Can one teach knowledge to God, since He judges those being high?
This one dies in the bone of his perfection, all of him at ease and at rest;
his pails are full of milk, and the marrow of his bones is moist.
And this one dies bitter in soul, and not having eaten of the good.
Together upon the dust they lie down, and the worm covers them over.
Behold, I know your⁺ thoughts, and the notions you⁺ wrest upon me.
For you⁺ say, ‘Where [is] the house of the noble? And where [is] the tent of the habitation of the wicked?’
Have you⁺ not asked those passing along the way, and do you⁺ not recognize their signs,
that from a day of calamity the evil one is held back, [and] in the day of wrath they are brought forth?
Who shall declare his way to his face? And who will repay him [for] what he has done?
When he is brought along to the graves, then one keeps watch over [his] tomb.
The clods of the torrent are sweet to him; and after him every man will extend, and those before his face are without number.
And how can you⁺ comfort me in vain, and in your⁺ answers remains falsehood?”
